newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Sept 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Sept 15.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
SUNDAY TELEGRAPH
-- PENNANT-REA'S HMSO STAKE

Rupert Pennant-Rea, former Bank of England governor, and fellow directors are expected to put up between 250,000 stg and 750,000 stg for equity stakes in the 125 million stg HMSO management buy-out which they run. Electra Fleming, the venture capital group leading the winning consortium called National Publishing Group, declined to say whether any of its staff who run the investment side will be taking an HMSO equity stake alongside their own funds.
-- SIMONDS QUITS HOTELS GROUP

Joint managing director of the Inter-Continental Hotels chain, Gavin Simonds, resigned yesterday, saying he had serious disagreements with the group's Japanese owner, Saison. His resignation is thought to signal an end to the international hotel group's plans for a float.
-- FOOTSIE PREPARES TO PASS 4000 MARK

The London stock market roared ahead to a record last week and is within sight of the 4000 mark. This is the 18th record- breaking session of the year. The FT-SE 100 index of leading stocks added 35.3 points to 3967.9 as buying, which had been selective earlier in the week, was seen across the board.
-- WEMBLEY STAKES CLAIM FOR NATIONAL STADIUM

Wembley, owner of the football stadium, has announced a return to the black at the half-year stage. The company has improved its chances of winning the right to build a new national stadium with 100 million stg of National Lottery money. Claes Hultman, chief executive, says an announcement is expected from the Sports Council by the end of the year.
-- CHARMAN OFFER TO NAMES WITHDRAWN

It has emerged that Charman, the underwriting agency run by John Charman, deputy chairman of Lloyd's, has withdrawn an offer to buy capacity from Names after members' rejected the proposals as inadequate. Charman had proposed acquiring capacity on its 300 million stg marine and energy Syndicate 488, one of the most successful in the market, from its 2,000 individual members. Members' agents rejected the proposals. Mr Charman accused individual Names of being anachronistic, saying that policyholders are looking for the solidity that big corporate backers provide.
SUNDAY TIMES
-- BUSINESSMEN OPPOSE A SINGLE CURRENCY

According to a survey of directors of almost 400 stock- market companies by Hemmington Scott, Britain's businessmen are strongly against a single European currency and believe it would push up unemployment, taxes and interest rates. It shows that Britain's directors are far more sceptical about the single currency than their European counterparts.
-- HUNT IS ON FOR MGAM NEW BROOM

Deutsche Bank is looking for an outsider to head Morgan Grenfell Asset Management, even if top managers are absolved from responsibility for the Peter Young European unit-trust controversy. If senior managers are implicated as a result of the internal investigation there will be a total clear-out of executives.
-- BA AIMS TO BE 'VIRTUAL AIRLINE'

British Airways is set to announce a blueprint for transforming itself into a "virtual airline" before the year 2000. The plan is to be presented to staff and union representatives on Wednesday and will provide for contracting out all its support services in a move that could reduce its workforce by 30,000.
-- BTR BOARD SHAKE-UP SOUGHT OVER DISPOSAL

After the huge reorganisation package at BTR, including a 35 per cent dividend cut and a 622 million stg write-off, fund managers and analysts expect a sweeping shake-up of BTR's board. Many of its executive directors may step down in the next year. Several big investors believe non-executive changes are vital if chief executive Ian Strachan is to push through his planned transformation of the group into a business focussed on global engineering businesses.
-- HSBC TO SPONSOR STEWART FOR 25 MILLION STG IN FORMULA ONE

HSBC Holdings, the banking group and owner of Midland Bank, is set to sign a 25 million stg sponsoring deal with Stewart Grand Prix, the Formula One motor racing team headed by Jackie Stewart. Marketing consultants say the deal matches perfectly with HSBC's promotional needs.
THE OBSERVER
-- 3.5 MILLION DOLLAR PAYOFF IN MORGAN OIL DEAL

It has been revealed that former fund manager of Morgan Grenfell Peter Young had arranged for the Luxembourg company Russ Oil and Technology to receive 3.5 million dollars worth of shares in Xavier Corporation, a little-known American oil exploration company in return for a 20 million dollar investment by one of the bank's funds.
-- TREASURY CONTRACT SPARKS LEGAL ROW

Godfrey Bradman, the controversial property developer who owns Whitehall Corporation, is preparing to sue the Government after failing to win a contract to redevelop the Treasury headquarters in Whitehall. He believes the bid, which cost one million stg to prepare was not treated fairly. The contract was given to Exchequer Partnership on Friday.
-- KVAERNER OFFERS 'FREE' THAMES BRIDGE

Kvaerner, the Norwegian engineering giant and builder of the Thames crossing, Dartford Bridge, is in talks with Government ministers and the Department of Transport with the intention of building another river crossing for free. It has presented a detailed plan in which it would pay for its 350 million stg construction by continuing to collect toll money from Dartford Bridge.
-- LLOYDS SUCCESSION WAR COMES INTO OPEN

Lloyds TSB is expected to announce that Sir Brian Pitman, chief executive, will become chairman. The succession has been an important issue for the group since 1991, when the board asked Sir Brian to stay on until the end of this year. Current chairman Sir Robin Ibbs has said he will retire by the next annual meeting in the spring.
-- CHANNEL FIVE REACHES FOR SKY TO BOOST AUDIENCE

Channel Five, the new television station due to be launched in January, is negotiating to become the first mainstream broadcaster to have its programmes carried on BSkyB's service. Both sides agree in principle and are deciding whether the additional coverage should be free to dish owners, or part of BSkyB's basic, paid-for package.
INDEPENDENT ON SUNDAY
-- CITY SEEKS BLOOD AT CIDER FIRM

The shock profits warning which wiped 270 million stg off the share price of the Taunton Cider to Babycham drinks maker, Matthew Clark, has led institutions to push for top management changes at the group. Chief executive Peter Aikens was still in meetings with City shareholders on Friday. The group blamed the sudden gloom on a dramatic collapse in July and August due to the success of new alcoholic soft drinks.
-- VIRGIN PLANS NEW US AIRLINE

If the Government can negotiate an open skies agreement to give British carriers the right to serve the American domestic market, Richard Branson will launch a US version of his Virgin Express short-haul low-cost European service early next year. The negotiations over a new open skies agreement are at present deadlocked but Virgin is pressing the Government to ignore pressures to settle for a weak US-style open skies agreement.
-- REVENUE BACKING BOOSTS EXCLUSIVE SALE

Granada has secured crucial Inland Revenue approval for the corporate structure of the Exclusive hotels chain which it put up for sale following the takeover of Forte FTE.L earlier this year. Approval is important because it gives Granada more flexibility over the disposal. The group can now either sell the chain as a single entity or as individual properties and still receive similar capital gains tax treatment.
-- BANK TO SHOW CITY IS HARD AT WORK ON EMU

The Bank of England will publish a document on Monday which will set out in detail the practical progress made to prepare the City for the introduction of a single currency. The document will be highly technical and will be heralded by the Bank as clear evidence that the City is doing all that is required to ready itself for monetary union, whether or not Britain is signed up for a single currency from the outset.
-- TORIES IN ROW OVER DOLE FIGURE 'FIDDLE'

Chancellor Kenneth Clarke will announce in October whether a new version of the monthly figures for unemployment should be introduced. The plan is to bring in a monthly labour force survey (LFS). Change will face opposition from Treasury officials and Gillian Shephard, Secretary of State at the Department for Education and Employment.
MAIL ON SUNDAY
-- NOMURA AIMS TO PLAY WITH OWN TRAIN SET

Nomura, the Japanese investment bank, is planning an offensive on Britain's newly privatised rail industry. Nomura joined a consortium last year that paid 700 million stg for Angel, one of three privatised rolling-stock leasing companies. The transaction was purely financial, however, the bank now plans to run its own slice of the rail network in the wake of the 825 million stg sale of rolling-stock leasing company Porterbrook.
-- SIX-FIGURE FINE FOR BREACHES AT NEWTON

One of the UK's most successful independent fund managers, Newton Investment Management, is facing a six-figure fine from the City's Investment Management Regulatory Organisation. The penalty is imposed for rule breaches relating to its institutional business.
-- P AND O AND BRITTANY PLOT CUT IN FERRY SERVICES

P&O, the UK ferry company, and Brittany, its French rival, are drawing up a deal to cut cross-Channel services in a move which will increase fares. The two groups will cut crossings on the Portsmouth to France routes and pool revenues from the new- look service. Operators want to cut capacity due to competition from Eurotunnel.
-- BUPA AND PPP HUNT PARTNERS FOR HEALTH

Leaders in the 1.6 billion stg health insurance market, BUPA and PPP Healthcare, are seeking major distribution partners in the wake of Abbey National's tie-up with Norwich Union. PPP is in talks with the Liverpool and Victoria friendly society. The talks between Abbey and Bupa broke down because Bupa was unwilling to give up its brand name, unlike Norwich.
-- FEARS ON TWO-TIER MARKET

The Stock Exchange is close to finalising plans for order- driven trading, which could insist on minimum orders of 4,000 stg, compared with the average private-client sum of 2,800 stg. This will lead to thousands of small shareholders being squeezed out of the London stock market.
